subject: Dedicated GPU pool pressure — request for exec attention & mitigation timeline
messages:
From: Amy Cheng <amy@acme.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Li <j.li@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 22:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool — urgent

Hi Olga,

We started seeing a ~40% drop in sustained throughput on our dedicated pool around 20:45 PDT last night. Requests are queuing and some batch jobs are timing out; error rate climbed from 0.2% to ~3.5%. This is impacting our real-time inference pipeline for vision tasks.

Can your team confirm whether this is capacity saturation on your end or something in our config? We need a short/medium-term mitigation plan and to understand if we should expect reduced SLAs.

We've attached a short CSV of per-queue latency and a screenshot of traces. Please advise next steps and when we can expect an update.

—Amy
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Robotics

[attachment: pool-usage-2026-07-31.csv] [attachment: latency-trace-0701.png]

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Cheng <amy@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 22:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool — urgent

Amy — thanks for the data. We're looking into it now. Initial read: the dedicated GPU pool assigned to Acme shows sustained utilization spikes above the configured max utilization window and our autoscaler did not bring additional reserved lanes due to an upstream scheduling throttling rule.

Immediate next steps:
- I'm escalating to infra on-call (Vivek is looped).
- We'll provision a short burst lane (non-reserved) to relieve the queue while we root-cause the scheduler behavior.
- Sending an initial incident bulletin in 30 minutes with ETA for mitigation.

Can you confirm whether you pushed any larger model variants or increased batch sizes around 20:30 PDT? That will help scope whether it's traffic pattern or model change.

Olga
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

[attachment: proposed-playbook-v1.docx]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 00:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool — urgent

On Fri, Jul 31, 2026 at 10:38 PM Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Amy — thanks for the data. We're looking into it now. Initial read: the dedicated GPU pool assigned to Acme shows sustained utilization spikes above the configured max utilization window and our autoscaler did not bring additional reserved lanes due to an upstream scheduling throttling rule.

Quick summary from infra triage:
- Cause: scheduler-level backpressure from a mis-evaluated affinity rule that prevented burst bands from being assigned to the pool.
- Impact: sustained queue growth for 17 minutes, peak token-per-second fall by ~38%.
- Workaround applied at 23:50 PDT: we disabled the offending affinity check and manually injected two burst lanes (NVIDIA A100-80GB equivalent) — queue drained, error rate returned to baseline.

Risks & next steps:
1) Need a rollback-safe scheduler patch and test run — target staging validation by EOD Monday.
2) Customer wants reimbursement consideration for missed throughput guarantees; I'll draft impact numbers.
3) Recommend a temporary runbook change to allow immediate auto-burst until patch lands.

I'm scheduling a 9:00 AM PDT sync with Olivia/CS and Acme to present the timeline and compensatory options. Olga, please join and bring the proposed playbook.

—Vivek
VP, Infrastructure

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 02:14:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool — urgent

Thanks team — good triage. A few items I want captured for the exec note:
- Quantify customer impact (tokens / minute, estimated revenue exposure for SLA breach window).
- Proposed customer-facing language and compensation band (credits % / discretionary engineering hours).
- Timing for permanent fix and canary schedule.

Jonas, Markus — please pull the usage metrics for the Acme pool (48-hour window) and confirm the peak sustained utilization metric and whether any other dedicated pools had correlated affinity hits. Attach to the exec brief.

I'll draft the external message and the internal exec one once I have numbers. Olga — prioritize the customer sync calendar invite.

Marissa
Director, CS Operations

From: Amy Cheng <amy@acme.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Li <j.li@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 05:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool — urgent

Thanks for the quick response and the burst lanes — throughput is back to normal. For context, we did deploy a heavier decoding model at 20:15 PDT and increased request concurrency for a pilot that ran through 22:00. We alerted the CS playbook but assumed dedicated autoscaling would absorb the load.

We appreciate the mitigation. We need clarity on:
- Whether this could recur on future pilot pushes.
- Formal SLA impact statement and proposed credits.
- A timeline for the scheduler fix.

We'd also like a short postmortem and the playbook you plan to use if this happens again. Happy to join a 9:00 AM PDT call.

—Amy

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Cheng <amy@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool — urgent

Amy — understood. Agenda for 9:00 AM PDT customer call:
1) Recap incident timeline & immediate mitigation.
2) Confirm Acme changes that contributed (model variant + concurrency).
3) Present short-term guardrail: auto-burst allowance + optional temporary throughput cap we can enable on push windows.
4) Compensation options (credit bands) and acceptance criteria.
5) Permanent fix timeline: scheduler patch -> staging canary -> production rollout (target: patch PR by Mon EOD, canary Tue morning, prod Wed night).

Internal asks: Jonas/Markus — bring the 48-hour utilization export and the token/sec numbers. Vivek — be prepared to explain rollback plan and test gating. Marissa — I'd like your draft exec note after the call so we can brief Sales + Legal.

Olga

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool — urgent

Attached export and quick findings:
- 48-hour window shows three micro-peak events across Acme's pool; only the 20:45 event aligns with model variant push and concurrency increase. Peak sustained util: 94% for 18 minutes.
- No other dedicated pools showed the scheduler-affinity issue during the same window.
- Attached CSV contains token/sec per-minute, error rate, and queue depth.

I'll join the 9:00 AM PDT call with these numbers and the trace images.

Jonas
Senior SRE
